title: Bob Carroll and the fake fights of New York tenor players
summary: Budd recalls tenor Bob Carroll, who staged fake bar fights with Ben Webster and others and was ruined by drink.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I see. Well, let's name some more New York saxophone players.
Bob Carroll. Bob Carroll was a beautiful saxophone player.
Big, tall, burly cat, and I tell you something about Bob Carroll and --
Bob Carroll, Ben Webster and Bob Darcy Dossey, they used to pull some funny things in New York. They all could blow their cans off. But you know what they used to do?
They would have for fun -- they would go in a tavern and pull a fake fight, and Tad would join up --

-- and they would actually be fighting each other like -- they would be playing, but they would be hitting, trying to knock each other out and beat each other up, and when they got through, they would be wrecking the joint. Bob Carroll, he played the last band that I know Bob Carroll played with was Willie Bryant's Bride's band in New York, and he could really blow the tenor saxophone. In fact, I thought he was going to be up in the class with another Chu Berry and whatnot, that's how much talent he had.
Yeah, his drinking sort of done him in.
